Overview

Magari runs the finances of a truck fleet. Drivers ask for fuel money from their phone, the vehicle manager approves it, the factory manager authorises it, and the accountant pays it out and attaches the receipt. Along the way the app measures fuel economy per car and per driver, keeps every car's profit or loss, and turns it all into reports the director can download.

  • 5roles, each with its own workspace
  • 4steps from request to receipt
  • 2report formats: PDF and Excel
  • 25entries per page on long histories

What it does

01Fuel requests that do the maths

The driver enters the odometer, the gauge, the station's price and the litres. The amount is worked out for them.

02A clear approval chain

The manager approves, the factory manager authorises, and the accountant pays with an M-Pesa reference, then adds a photo of the receipt.

03Profit or loss per car

Income per trip, cargo priced by the tonne or by the kilo, set against every shilling spent on that car.

04Fuel economy, measured

Kilometres, litres, km per litre and TSh per km, by car and by driver, worked out from real readings.

05Reports worth sending

Per car, month or week, as a PDF or an Excel workbook with live formulas, tables and native charts.

06Invoices (ankara)

Trips priced per tonne or per kilo, with payment details, ready to hand to the customer.

On the screen

For the technical reader

How it's built

  • Next.js
  • TypeScript
  • PostgreSQL
  • Pusher
  • React PDF
  • ExcelJS
  1. Next.js App Router, with server-only data access to PostgreSQL.
  2. Live updates through Pusher: an approval appears on the next person's screen straight away.
  3. Excel workbooks with native charts from ExcelJS. PDFs from React PDF.
  4. Drivers sign in with their plate number, staff with email. Passwords hashed with bcrypt.
  5. Installable as an app on Android and desktop.
